Element.attribute: Define entry and exit criteria and acceptance thresholds
Define entry and exit criteria and acceptance thresholds

For each test level and type, define the entry and exit criteria, which determine start and stop points in test execution. Entry criteria requires that the proper environment is in place to support the upcoming test cycle. Exit criteria require that the solution under test has been satisfactorily completed before exiting the test level/type. To define entry and exit criteria, consideration must be given to the conditions which must be satisfied before test execution can begin and when test execution can end. Entry and exit criteria should consider situations where time constraints necessitate overlapping test cycles.

Stakeholder consensus on entry and exit criteria prior to test execution is essential for successful and timely completion of test effort. In conjunction with exit criteria, acceptance criteria for discovered defects is commonly discussed with stakeholders. Acceptance criteria defines a tolerance level for defects that allows the test team to continue with the test effort should certain defects remain outstanding at the conclusion of a test type.

Perform the following:

  • Identify relevant test cycle
  • Conduct risk assessment session with key stakeholders
  • Conduct statistical analysis of defect impact on overall solution integrity
  • Propose gate exit criteria
  • Review configuration dependencies
  • Review master data dependencies
  • Conduct defect impact assessment
  • Propose gate entry criteria
  • Review test gate entry and exit criteria with all stakeholders
  • Approve test gate entry and exit criteria
  • Define test execution suspension and resumption criteria

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute: Discuss with stakeholders communication routines to be used for each test type. The goal is to come up with the number of meetings required to address identified risks and issues throughout the testing lifecycle and for easy coordination amongst different groups participating in the test effort. The frequency (twice a day, once a day, twice a week, etc.) of the meetings should also be discussed with stakeholders to allow for structured communication during testing.  The frequency (monthly, weekly, daily, etc.) of status reporting should also be discussed with stakeholders.

Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute: Discuss with stakeholders the approach to conduct training on the target solution before test execution begins. Training provides testers with a holistic understanding of the target solution needed to perform a comprehensive test. However, prioritizing certain components of the target solution may be required based on limitations due to test scope, time and cost associated with training. Priority should be given to key aspects of the target solution that pose a high risk of defects and thus require a large volume of testing to mitigate the risk.
